newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to issue T$5 bln NCDs on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to issue T$5 bln NCDs on Wednesday.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank said on Wednesday it would issue T$5 billion in 14-day negotiable certificates of deposit later in the day.
Bids would close at 15.00 local time (0700 GMT), a central bank official said.

The NCDs issue comes just two days after central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong on Monday pledged that the bank would take the economy's health into consideration in any further issues of the short-term instruments.
"We will not continue to blindly issue NCDs," Sheu said in the wake of the stock market's plunges on Monday. "We will do it in consideration of overall economic conditions."
The central bank had made major daily NCD issues almost every day up until March 21, reportedly trying to control loose liquidity that many analysts said was fuelling a stock market rally.
The last such intervention came on March 21, the same day that the stock market plunged more than three percent over a hog foot and mouth epidemic sweeping the island.
The stock market fell dramatically on Monday and Tuesday over the pork crisis, but was rebounding early on Wednesday.
